source_review.notes: Checked current official Apache Spark shuffle monitoring/configuration documentation; current Apache Flink metrics, backpressure, network-memory, and checkpoint guidance; current Linux interface-statistics documentation; current IETF TCP/congestion/window specifications; current Google Cloud and Amazon EC2 bandwidth documentation; and Apache Kafka 4.2 quota design. All thirteen final references returned HTTP 200. Runtime-, protocol-, kernel-, and provider-specific limits are attributed.

evidence: Reviewed flow/resource sets, per-flow path and rate, directed resource capacity/utilization, useful bytes/goodput/time, RTT/BDP, producer-consumer fan-out, overhead, and queue notation.
Checked that bits versus bytes, decimal Gbps/MB versus binary TiB/MiB, direction, capacity class, and time window are explicit in computations.
Checked that offered load, served throughput, application goodput, retransmitted/duplicate bytes, and committed output remain distinct.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The D/G expression is labeled as a lower bound, and utilization is meaningful only under matching direction, topology, tenant/class, and rate semantics.

evidence: Executed the Python 3 fixture and reproduced 100.0-Gbps capacity, 80.0-Gbps safe envelope, 35.0-Gbps baseline, 29.3-Gbps shuffle requirement, and 64.3-Gbps planned average.
Recomputed 12 TiB over 3,600 seconds as approximately 29.3203 Gbps using binary TiB and decimal Gbps.
Recomputed 100 Gbps times 2 ms as 25,000,000 bytes, equal to 25.00 MB or approximately 23.84 MiB BDP.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Average-envelope fit excludes protocol/retry overhead, microbursts, per-flow/PPS caps, endpoint limits, and variable effective goodput.

evidence: Verified directed resource utilization sums rates only for flows traversing the resource and divides by capacity available to that class/direction/window.
Verified any topology cut bounds aggregate traffic crossing it even when individual worker links appear unconstrained.
Verified bounded queues under overload drain only when backpressure/admission makes offered load lower than service for sufficient time; more buffers do not change steady-state capacity.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: BDP estimates useful in-flight data for path filling but do not prescribe socket buffers or guarantee congestion-window, receiver-window, or application throughput.

evidence: Reviewed empty/tiny/huge blocks, few elephants, many mice, all-to-all fan-out, one hot receiver, synchronized reducer waves, and skew.
Reviewed low/high RTT, loss, ECN, queue/RX drops, per-flow/aggregate/PPS caps, cross-rack/zone routes, noisy tenants, and receiver CPU/disk limits.
Reviewed retries, speculation, timeout oscillation, worker/rack loss, checkpoint/control traffic, recovery catch-up, compression, and isolated-versus-shared benchmark cohorts.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: The chapter treats byte saturation, packet/request saturation, endpoint starvation, and shared-cut saturation as different failure surfaces.

evidence: Traced logical records through serialization/compression, local/remote shuffle, physical interface traffic, retransmission/retry/speculation, and one-winner committed output.
Checked bounded transfer admission/backpressure, reserved control/checkpoint/recovery capacity, timeout/backoff behavior, and retry budgets.
Checked record/key/order/state/output, integrity/authentication, topology failure-domain, and degraded-recovery invariants under byte-reduction and placement changes.
invariant_checking.notes: Performance relief is not accepted if it weakens dataflow semantics, liveness/control traffic, security, rollback, or failure independence.

evidence: Reviewed cut-capacity reasoning across worker, rack, zone, virtual-instance, shuffle-service, and destination resources.
Reviewed endpoint exclusion requirements before attributing a flat goodput ceiling to the network path.
Reviewed flow-conservation and backpressure-progress arguments with named protocol, retransmission, duplicate, retry, and unrelated-traffic residuals.
proof_review.notes: A link label, high/low utilization, flat throughput, backpressure, or loss alone is insufficient causal proof of the job's bottleneck.

evidence: Audited offered load, capacity, utilization, goodput, bottleneck, BDP, incast, elephant/mice flow, bisection bandwidth, backpressure, and congestion-signal terminology.
Confirmed worker NIC, NIC queues/PPS, instance aggregate/per-flow, rack/zone cut, gateway/service quota, shuffle service, receiver disk/CPU, and storage endpoint are distinct resources.
Confirmed network buffers, congestion/receive windows, application concurrency, transport retransmission, application retry, and speculative duplicate are separate mechanisms.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Provider-specific and engine-specific mechanisms are presented as concrete examples of the general directed-resource model.

evidence: Reviewed logical/shuffle/transferred/retransmitted bytes; block/request/flow/connection counts; directed goodput/utilization; RTT/queues; ECN/loss; and windows.
Reviewed NIC errors/drops/PPS/queues/CPU/interrupts, socket queues, fetch wait/backpressure, receiver disk/decode, retries/speculation, throttles, and cost.

Confirmed segmentation by execution identity, source/destination, interface/rack/zone/region, transport/class/tenant, block/flow cohort, tier/version/config, normal/recovery load, percentile, direction, and window.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Coarse averages and isolated benchmarks are explicitly insufficient for claims about microbursts, shared topology, degraded operation, or production tail behavior.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed directed traffic mapping, applicable capacity, burst windows, goodput, endpoint/path diagnosis, all-to-all amplification, BDP, congestion, queues/backpressure, byte reduction, shaping, topology, control traffic, timeouts, next bottlenecks, and observability.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed implementable cross-layer evidence, per-peer/rack admission, block batching, compression/locality experiments, reserved control capacity, timeout/backoff, provider-limit checks, degraded recovery, and end-to-end retesting. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from network resource vocabulary through cut/endpoint diagnosis to safe mitigations. Ten examples and five answered exercises cover safe envelopes, shuffle rate, BDP, fan-out, endpoint exclusion, microbursts, incast, placement, timeouts, capacity arithmetic, fetch control, experiments, and mitigation selection.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external Spark/Flink/Linux/IETF/cloud/Kafka maintainer, network/fabric/runtime/storage/platform/SRE/security/economics specialist, production operator, provider representative, downstream consumer, affected user, governance or accessibility specialist, or certification review is claimed.
